name: Shabelle Coast
inspired_by: Southern and central Somalia with northern elements, as of 2026: a coral-stone coastal capital-type city behind dunes, the irrigated Shabelle-type river corridor, vast Acacia-Commiphora bushland where al-Shabaab holds the countryside, dry limestone mountains in the north-east standing in for Puntland's Cal Miskaad range (IS-Somalia), and a foreign-hosted port enclave inspired by Djibouti's base cluster. All towns are fictional.
climate: Hot semi-arid (Koppen BSh) on the coast and river, arid (BWh) in the north-east mountains' lowlands. 27-35 C year-round on the coast with high humidity and sea breezes; inland up to 40 C. Two rainy seasons: Gu (April-June) and Deyr (October-November), 300-500 mm on the coast and river, under 200 mm in the north-east. Droughts and river floods both common.
seasons: Jilaal (Jan-Mar): long hot dry season, dust, herds at wells
Gu rains (Apr-Jun): main rains, river floods, muddy roads, green bush
Hagaa (Jul-Sep): cooler, windy south-west monsoon on the coast, light showers, rough seas
Deyr rains (Oct-Dec): short rains, second planting

vegetation: coconut and neem in the city
riverine forest of Ficus sycomorus and tamarind

terrain.relief: Coastal dune ridge (30-80 m) behind the beach; flat river corridor (50-150 m) running parallel to the coast; gently rising bushland plains (150-450 m) with low ridges; rugged limestone mountains in the north-east rising to 1,600 m with deep gorges (togga) and caves.
features: coral-stone old town on a headland
a perennial river running parallel to the coast and ending in swamps
terrain.water: Indian Ocean along the south-east edge and a gulf on the north-east edge (composite); one perennial river with seasonal floods; boreholes and berkads (cement rainwater cisterns) in the bush; gorge springs in the mountains.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m. Coastal ramp with a dune ridge (anisotropic noise along the shoreline), a flat river corridor carved as a spline basin 2-4 km wide, bushland plains of low fbm, and a north-east mountain block as ridged noise masked by distance, with gorges carved by flow accumulation. Sea and reef via bathymetry below 0 m.

noise_layers.purpose: inland rise of the bushland plains
north-east limestone mountains, masked to that corner
termite mounds scattered over bushland (instanced, not heightmap, at close range)

generator.erosion: Hydraulic erosion in the mountains (80 iterations) for gorges; bushland and river corridor kept flat; dunes shaped by the anisotropic layer only.
generator.rivers: River spline parallel to the coast 6-10 km inland, 30-60 m wide, ending in a swamp; canals branch to farms; dry riverbeds from the mountains by flow accumulation.
generator.settlement_flattening: City flattened on the dune back-slope; villages flattened as small discs; mountain hamlets per plot.
generator.notes: Bushland gives 30-150 m sightlines with thorn walls: ideal for ambush and for al-Shabaab movement. The main supply route from the city through the river corridor to inland towns (with two river bridges) is the key convoy line and the most-attacked road on the map.

settlements.architecture: Coastal city district: an old quarter of coral-stone and lime-plaster houses with carved wooden doors and flat roofs, partly ruined from decades of war; newer three- to ten-storey concrete hotels, offices and apartment blocks painted in pastel colours; blast walls and gates around hotels and ministries; markets of corrugated-iron stalls.
settlements.wall_class: Coral stone 50 cm thick; concrete frames thick; blast walls thick; stalls none.
layout_rules: old quarter on a headland with a lighthouse and mosques
grid of newer districts with paved and sand streets
fortified airport and international zone on the coast

settlements.architecture: Inland market town on the river or a road junction: one-storey stone and block houses with corrugated-iron roofs painted in bright colours, a mosque with a green dome, a market, a district office, an army base on the edge behind a sand berm.
settlements.wall_class: Block and stone medium; tin roofs none; base berm thick.
layout_rules: grid around a market and a mosque
river bridge or ford at one edge
army base and AU-type camp on the edge

settlements.architecture: Bush villages of round huts (mundul) with mud-and-wattle walls and conical thatch roofs, rectangular tin-roofed houses, thorn-fence livestock enclosures (zariba), a small mosque, a berkad cistern.
settlements.footprint_m: hut 4-5 m diameter; homestead 30x30 inside a thorn fence
settlements.wall_class: Wattle and mud 15-20 cm thin; thorn fences block movement but not fire.
layout_rules: loose cluster of homesteads around a well or cistern
tracks in from the road; bush all around

settlements.architecture: Displacement camps on the city edge: domed buul shelters of sticks, cloth and plastic sheeting, tin shacks, water points, aid distribution areas.
layout_rules: dense irregular clusters on open land
water tanks and latrines at intervals

settlements.architecture: Military and foreign compounds: Somali army forward bases (sand berm, container towers, technicals), an AU-type contingent base with HESCO, a Turkish-run training base with barracks blocks, foreign naval bases in the port enclave (fenced, hangars, quays), al-Shabaab bush camps.
settlements.footprint_m: forward base 200x200; training base 800x600; enclave base 1000x800
settlements.wall_class: Berms and HESCO thick; containers thin.
layout_rules: forward bases on the main supply route
enclave bases fenced along the port
bush camps hidden in thickets near water

infrastructure.roads: One paved main supply route from the city through the river corridor to inland towns (potholed, with two river bridges and many culverts), sand roads elsewhere, mountain tracks in the north-east. Al-Shabaab checkpoints tax the bush roads.
infrastructure.power: Private diesel and solar mini-grids in the city and towns; no national grid.
infrastructure.ports: City seaport with breakwater and quays; the foreign-hosted port enclave with naval quays; fishing beaches.
infrastructure.airfields: Fortified international airport in the city, an airbase inland used for drone and training operations, laterite strips at inland towns.
infrastructure.checkpoints: Army and police checkpoints on the city exits and the main supply route; AU-type contingent posts; al-Shabaab 'tax' checkpoints in the bush; clan militia checkpoints between districts.

conditions: rain squalls in the Gu and Deyr
windy monsoon months with rough seas
weather.visibility_notes: Bush limits sightlines more than weather; rain squalls ground drones briefly; rough seas in July-August stop small-boat operations.

civilians.behaviour: Busy city markets from dawn; khat deliveries arrive mid-morning; Friday prayers at midday; herders with camels and goats on all roads; minibus traffic between towns; in the bush, villagers live alongside al-Shabaab control and avoid any armed force. Civilians in the city shelter quickly after explosions and crowds gather afterwards.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: The city, camps and markets are very dense; bush zones are low density but villages lie inside them. Complex-attack defence near the city is where the casualty rule bites most.

factions_present.where: Acacia-Commiphora bushland and bush villages, river-corridor farms at night, tax checkpoints on bush roads; complex attacks on bases and the city.
North-east limestone mountains: cave bases and gorge camps (IS-Somalia).

frontline: Al-Shabaab holds most bush zones and pushes on the main supply route; the government holds the city, towns and bases. Army offensives (often with player contracts) retake towns, which become 'liberated' zones that must be held against counter-attacks for several campaign days or flip back. Al-Shabaab complex attacks on forward bases and city hotels are events that post defence and hostage contracts. In the north-east, IS-Somalia holds mountain cave zones that shrink under cell-hunt contracts. AU-type funding events can thin the AUSSOM-type contingent, weakening government hold on the river corridor. Piracy events post boarding and hostage contracts at sea.

hot_zones.name: Bushland belt
hot_zones.layout: al_shabaab HQ in a bush camp near a pond; 4-6 outposts in villages and thickets; tax checkpoints on bush roads; roaming technicals and foot patrols; 1-2 QRF of technicals; a government forward base on the edge as the friendly anchor

insertion.fob: LHD offshore for coastal, city and anti-piracy contracts (landing at the port or beach). Inland FOB at the drone airbase for bush contracts, reached by the main supply route or helicopter; AAVs usable on the coast and river corridor.

early_game_notes: al_shabaab and isis are early-tier; som is an early-game client. Rival PMCs (mid) appear in the north-east and city.
ambient_audio: weaver birds and hornbills in the bush
